s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent syncope with palpitations and transient loss of consciousness
salient_findings: Syncope with preceding palpitation and amaurosis
Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia during presyncope episode
Diffuse stenosis in proximal to mid-LAD and stenosis in mid-right coronary artery
key_facts: Previous episode of syncope 1 month prior
Normal vital signs and physical examination
Normal laboratory tests, including blood glucose, electrolytes, D-dimer, troponin I, and N-terminal pro–B-type natriuretic peptide
Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia recorded during 24-hour Holter monitoring
50% to 90% diffuse stenosis in proximal to mid-LAD
Minimum lumen area of 5.92 mm2 in proximal LAD, with plaque burden of 74%

shortlist.label: Coronary artery disease
shortlist.why_kept: Diffuse stenosis in proximal to mid-LAD and 80% stenosis in mid-right coronary artery

shortlist.label: Long QT syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: QTc of 403 milliseconds and polymorphic ventricular tachycardia recorded during 24-hour Holter monitoring

shortlist.label: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia recorded during 24-hour Holter monitoring

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent syncope and polymorphic ventricular tachycardia

shortlist.label: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Previous episode of syncope and family history of diabetes, which may be associated with cardiomyopathy

raw.rationale: The patient experienced polymorphic ventricular tachycardia during a presyncope episode, which is a characteristic feature of catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT). The normal electrocardiogram and echocardiography results, along with the presence of ventricular tachycardia during a Holter monitor, support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Coronary artery disease
rejected.why: While the patient has significant coronary artery disease, the presence of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia during a presyncope episode suggests a primary arrhythmic disorder rather than ischemia-induced syncope.

rejected.label: Long QT syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's QTc interval of 403 milliseconds is within the normal range, making long QT syndrome less likely.

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: There is no evidence of right ventricular dysfunction or structural abnormalities on the echocardiogram to support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The echocardiogram showed a normal left ventricular ejection fraction and no evidence of hypertrophy, making this diagnosis unlikely.
